title: Group: legal entity register, CAGE code list and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system
what_it_shows: A publicly traded holding company (SEC registrant) with three wholly owned operating subsidiaries, each with its own CAGE codes: Aircraft Parts (NAICS 336413; 9 plants), Engineering Services (NAICS 541330; 4 engineering centers) and Defense Software and Data Services (NAICS 513210). Corporate shared services (identity, network, security operations, cloud platform, ERP, HR, finance, legal, export compliance, internal audit) sit in the parent. Organization charts show the Group CISO, the Group CMMC program director reporting to the Group CISO, the Group Chief Risk Officer, the Group export compliance director, the Group ITPSO, the three division security and compliance leads and the division presidents as CMMC Affirming Officials for their CAGE codes

title: Group: HR roster by division
source_system: Group HR system (HR SaaS)
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees: Aircraft Parts about 25,500, Engineering Services about 10,800 (about 1,200 of them engineers working on customer sites), Defense Software about 4,700, corporate shared services about 4,000. Termination and transfer events feed SYS-G1 identity governance

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger; FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Revenue of about $18.0 billion: Aircraft Parts about $11.4 billion (about 55% defense work: DoD spares and sustainment contracts and subcontracts under four airframe prime contractors, Primes A to D; the rest commercial aerospace), Engineering Services about $4.8 billion, Defense Software about $1.8 billion. Aircraft Parts ships on about 250 production days a year

title: Group: FY2025 Form 10-K Item 106 disclosure and disclosure committee charter
source_system: SEC filings; corporate secretary's records
what_it_shows: The FY2025 annual report includes the Regulation S-K Item 106 description of cyber risk management, strategy and governance (board audit and risk committee oversight; the Group CISO's reporting line). The disclosure committee charter includes materiality decisions on cybersecurity incidents for Form 8-K Item 1.05; incident facts reach the committee from the Group CISO

title: Group: contract clause inventory and clause library
source_system: Group legal contract management system
what_it_shows: Aircraft Parts and Engineering Services DoD prime contracts and subcontracts (including subcontracts under Primes A to D) carry DFARS 252.204-7012 (MAY 2024), 252.204-7019 and 252.204-7020 (NOV 2023), FAR 52.204-21 (NOV 2021) and FAR 52.204-25; awards made from 2025-11-10 also carry DFARS 252.204-7021 (NOV 2025). Defense Software DoD edition contracts carry DFARS 252.239-7010 (JAN 2023) and 252.204-7012. The clause library holds 2025 flowdown templates for purchase orders and subconsultant agreements and the security, U.S.-person and DFARS terms used in contracts for GCEE services

title: Group: DoD program office and prime contractor notices on CMMC levels
source_system: Contracts correspondence files (Group CMMC program office)
what_it_shows: DoD program offices and Primes A to D told the group that solicitations issued from 2026-11-10 (CMMC Phase 2) would require CMMC Level 2 (C3PAO) for CUI work. The Program H program office told Aircraft Parts to expect Level 3 (DIBCAC) from Phase 3 (2027-11-10)

title: Group: SPRS records and 2024 DIBCAC assessment file
source_system: Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS); Group CMMC program office files
what_it_shows: DCMA DIBCAC High Assessment of the Aircraft Parts CUI environment (fieldwork 2024-05-13 to 2024-05-24), score 98, posted 2024-06-07; Engineering Services Basic Assessment, score 101, posted 2025-03. No CMMC status is recorded for any group CAGE code, and no Phase 1 award to the group has required Level 2 (Self). The 2024 assessment file holds the records the group supplied to the assessors

title: Group: CMMC program office charter and planned assessment scope
source_system: Group CMMC program office records
what_it_shows: The CMMC program office reports to the Group CISO and coordinates scopes, SPRS submissions and C3PAO and DIBCAC contacts. The planned Level 2 assessment scope is one Enterprise CUI Environment: the GCEE, plants 1 to 8 and the Engineering Services centers. Plant 9 is outside it until its migration into the GCEE (due 2027-03-31). The staffing plan lists the CMMC specialists the divisions share

title: Group: policy and standards library (2025)
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: Group policies (2025) aligned to NIST CSF 2.0, with group standards for identity and passwords, logging, remote access, wireless, telework, mobile devices, training, VoIP, conference rooms, CUI transport, procurement and the export tag policy. The library has no AI standard and no cyber due diligence standard for acquisitions

title: Group: division supplements and policy register
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: Engineering Services supplement v2024, last aligned to group policy in 2024-05, with no owner or review date; no 2025 review is recorded. It allows personal cloud sync for non-CUI data and unregistered drives on customer test systems at customer request, which differ from the group standards on removable media and cloud storage. Defense Software supplement v2025, aligned 2025-10, with no data-use gate for Government-related data and no CSP reporting procedure for SYS-D4 tenants. The Aircraft Parts supplement is on file

title: Group: common control catalog and inheritance matrices
source_system: GRC tool
what_it_shows: The common control catalog lists the controls corporate provides (SYS-G1, SYS-G2, SYS-G3, group HR, supply chain, facilities and the CMMC program office). Inheritance is documented for Aircraft Parts (2025 inheritance matrix and plant enclave SSPs), for Defense Software (DoD edition SSP; industry edition SOC 2 system description) and for the Engineering Services centers. No inheritance record covers the Engineering Services HPC cluster and test systems, which joined the CUI environment in 2026

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication policy, methods report and sign-in settings
source_system: SYS-G1 admin consoles (government-community and commercial tenants)
what_it_shows: Two tenants: a government-community tenant for every CUI environment, which requires a verified U.S.-person attribute before any CUI group, and a commercial tenant for other workforce use. MFA is required for every CUI user; 64% use phishing-resistant authenticators and the rest number-matching push. Administrators use hardware security keys. Lockout after 10 failed attempts with risk-based blocking; sessions end after 15 minutes idle on CAD virtual workstations, 30 minutes in the PLM web client, or 12 hours; passwords of at least 14 characters with banned-password checks and no reuse of the last 24; replay-resistant federation with signed tokens; obscured sign-in feedback; a CUI banner at sign-in. Global administrator roles exist in the government-community tenant

title: Group: SYS-G1 identity governance configuration, inactive account report and service account register
source_system: SYS-G1 identity governance module
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows run from HR events; access to CUI groups needs the U.S.-person attribute recorded by export compliance; accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically, with a monthly report to the GCEE platform lead; account events go to the SIEM; identifiers are not reused for 3 years. The GCEE has about 12,600 named users (6,900 Aircraft Parts, 5,200 Engineering Services, 120 Defense Software, 380 corporate) and 140 service accounts, listed in a separate service account register

title: Group: privileged access management policy, account register, session logs and secrets vault
source_system: PAM console; secrets vault
what_it_shows: Privileged access is just in time through PAM with approval and session recording; administrators use separate privileged accounts that cannot read email or browse the internet; privileged roles are listed in a role register (6 SOC engineers can change log settings); every privileged session and command goes to the SIEM; PLM vendor maintenance runs only through PAM with named accounts and MFA, and vendor personnel without U.S.-person verification get supervised sessions only; maintenance tools are listed in a tool register; service secrets are kept in the vault

title: Group: Q1 2026 access certification results
source_system: SYS-G1 identity governance module
what_it_shows: Quarterly certification of project roles by project data owners and of privileged roles by the GCEE system owner completed for Q1 2026

title: Group: endpoint configuration baseline, device control policy and software catalog
source_system: Endpoint management and device control consoles; software catalog
what_it_shows: Virtual and thick CAD workstations lock after 15 minutes with a pattern-hiding screen and enforce application allow-listing. Virtual workstations are non-persistent and block download, clipboard, print and removable media; on thick workstations device control allows only registered, hardware-encrypted, company-issued drives. Laptops have full-disk encryption with FIPS-validated modules; mobile devices reach only the CUI suite app with app protection. Software comes from a self-service catalog that includes CAD plug-ins; browser policy restricts mobile code. Web category blocks for public AI services apply on GCEE virtual workstations; not all company laptops, including developer laptops, are covered

title: Group: SIEM data source inventory, use case catalog and health rules
source_system: SIEM (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: In-house 24x7 SOC with the SIEM hosted in the government-community cloud. Sources include GCEE components, SYS-G1, PAM, the exchange gateway, EDR, the provider A hub, SYS-D3 and SYS-D4 infrastructure and application logs, the HPC network segment, and MES and DNC logs from plants 1, 2, 3 and 5. MES and DNC logs at plants 4, 6, 7 and 8 stay on local servers for 30 days; HPC host and scheduler logs and the predictive model service logs are not sources. Health alerts fire when a GCEE source stops sending for 30 minutes; plant sources have no health alert. Use cases cover mass download, off-hours project access, export-tag violations, remote access, identity events and unusual tenant access, with weekly review reports and case records; PLM and gateway download alerts use one group-wide threshold for every project

title: Group: IR plan v4, SOC case export, exercise reports and notification matrix
source_system: SOC case management; group policy repository; exercise library
what_it_shows: Group IR plan v4, approved by the Group CISO and reviewed each year, with playbooks, a forensic retainer with on-site terms, an incident response team roster, DC3 malware submission and image preservation steps, and a step for prime notices; cases are tracked in the SOC case system with triage and severity. Technical playbooks are exercised quarterly, including a GCEE data-theft scenario in 2026-04. The group notification matrix lists DoD, prime, customer, export, NISPOM and SEC duties; it has not been exercised, and exercises to date are technical

title: Group: DIBNet certificate register and drill record
source_system: Group CMMC program office; incident binder
what_it_shows: DoD-approved medium assurance certificate holders: Aircraft Parts 4 (the director of contracts and 3 others), Engineering Services 2 (both at one center), Defense Software none; certificates are checked quarterly. Aircraft Parts reporters ran a DIBNet drill in 2026-03. Certificate holders keep clean laptops and printed contact lists in the incident binder

title: Group: EDR coverage report
source_system: EDR console
what_it_shows: EDR with anti-malware runs on all managed endpoints, servers, virtual and thick workstations and the SYS-D3, SYS-D4 and SYS-D5 workloads, with automatic updates, real-time and periodic scans, and scanning of diagnostic media before use. Plant 9 endpoints have been enrolled since 2026-02

title: Group: vulnerability scan, remediation and patch reports and control health dashboard, Q1 2026
source_system: Vulnerability scanner; patch management; GRC dashboard
what_it_shows: Authenticated vulnerability scans run weekly on the GCEE and plants 1 to 8; Plant 9 is not in the scan schedule. Remediation metrics track critical findings to 14 days and high to 30 days. GCEE servers and virtual workstation images are patched monthly, with critical patches in 14 days. A monthly control health dashboard reports identity, patching, scanning and logging coverage to the Group CISO

title: Group: threat intelligence log, SOC service catalog and staffing roster
source_system: SOC knowledge base
what_it_shows: Security advisories and DoD DIB threat sharing feed the SOC and the patch process; the SOC service catalog lists incident support to division teams; the staffing roster covers 24x7 operation by in-house analysts

title: Group: cloud account inventory and IAM export, providers A and B
source_system: Cloud provider consoles (providers A and B)
what_it_shows: Provider A's government-community landing zone (an offering FedRAMP authorized at High) hosts the GCEE, the Program H account, SYS-D3, SYS-D4, the SYS-D5 runners, the SIEM and the HPC burst service; provider B's commercial landing zone hosts non-CUI corporate workloads only. Cloud roles are federated from SYS-G1 with no long-lived cloud user keys. Paired-region failover is configured for the GCEE; SYS-D3 and SYS-D4 have warm standby regions. Asset and tenant inventories come from cloud tooling

title: Group: landing-zone guardrail, data loss and drift reports
source_system: Guardrail policy service
what_it_shows: Organization policies enforce approved regions, encryption, logging and an approved-service list in every division account; drift is reported daily; provider B guardrails and data loss rules block CUI

title: Group: network design, firewall and security group exports and VPN configuration
source_system: Firewall management; network documentation
what_it_shows: The provider A hub controls traffic into and out of the GCEE, SYS-D3 and SYS-D4 with deny by default; PLM has no public endpoint; the exchange gateway sits in its own DMZ subnet; administration uses PAM and separate management subnets; WAF and DDoS protection at the hub. Remote access is through the virtual desktop gateway or the group VPN, with split tunneling disabled; plant and center VPNs for plants 1 to 8 and all centers terminate on FIPS-validated gateways; TLS protects sessions. Plants 1 to 8 have a second carrier and engineering centers cellular backup. Wireless at plants and centers uses WPA3-Enterprise with certificates. External connections are listed in a connection register. Systems use the provider time service and group time servers

title: Group: key management configuration, key age report and FIPS module certificate list
source_system: Key management service (provider A)
what_it_shows: Customer-managed keys in an HSM-backed key service, with separate keys per account (GCEE, Program H, SYS-D3, SYS-D4), rotated yearly; CUI in storage, databases and backups is encrypted. The module certificate list shows FIPS-validated modules for CUI encryption at rest and in transit, including the virtual desktop gateway. The key age report lists GCEE service account keys by age against a 90-day rotation rule

title: Group: backup policy, immutable vault configuration and backup job reports, Q1 2026
source_system: Backup service (provider A)
what_it_shows: An immutable backup vault in a second provider A region inside the government-community offering, with a separate backup identity: hourly GCEE vault snapshots with continuous database replication, daily SYS-D3 and SYS-D4 backups, and nightly MES backups from plants 1 to 8, encrypted with customer-managed keys. Q1 2026 job reports show completed jobs

title: Group: log archive immutability and retention settings
source_system: SIEM and central log archive account
what_it_shows: Logs are kept 1 year online in the SIEM and 3 years in an immutable archive; only SOC engineering roles can change log settings

title: Group: training, phishing simulation and acknowledgment records
source_system: Group learning system; HR acknowledgment records
what_it_shows: Annual security awareness training with phishing simulations covering CUI handling and export control, with 97% completion for the current cycle; role-based training for PLM administrators, platform engineers, export-tag owners, incident responders, division reporters and field engineers; insider threat awareness training for all GCEE users; rules of behavior, nondisclosure and export control acknowledgments signed at onboarding and each year

title: Group: HR screening, U.S.-person verification, termination and transfer records
source_system: Group HR system; export compliance verification log; contractor register
what_it_shows: Background screening at hire and U.S.-person verification by export compliance before any CUI access; terminations disable access within 4 hours (immediately for involuntary) and transfers trigger a role review within 5 business days; contractors follow the same rules through their sponsors; positions are risk-designated, with GCEE administrator roles high risk; notice-period monitoring of departing staff is manual; Engineering Services departures include GFE return confirmation with the customer

title: Group: insider threat program plan and referral log
source_system: Insider threat program office
what_it_shows: One entity-wide insider threat program for the cleared entities under the Group ITPSO (32 CFR 117.7(b)(4)(iii)), with training, referrals and SOC analytics; accounts flagged by the program or HR are disabled within 1 hour of the request

title: Group: export compliance program records
source_system: Group export compliance office
what_it_shows: DDTC registration statements current for Aircraft Parts and Engineering Services (22 CFR 122.1); technical assistance agreements and licenses in the agreement register; Empowered Officials named in both divisions; sharing approvals for allied partners. The export compliance procedure keeps CUI in U.S. government-community regions with U.S.-person gating and does not rely on the encrypted-data carve-out. Commercial parts carry EAR-controlled technology. Public releases go through the public release review log. Project folders shared with allied partners are not tagged with the agreement that authorizes them

title: Group: accounts payable vendor master, supplier verification report and SCRM plan
source_system: ERP vendor master; supplier risk tool; SCRM plan
what_it_shows: About 1,450 suppliers and outside processors receive CUI through the exchange gateway. The supplier verification report shows CMMC status verified for 38% of the suppliers that would have needed Level 2 (C3PAO) on Phase 2 subcontracts; an SPRS check has been part of supplier onboarding since 2025, and legacy suppliers have not been rechecked; new orders since 2025-11-10 carry 252.204-7021. The SCRM plan covers IT and engineering services suppliers, not machine and controller suppliers. The vendor master lists the cloud, SaaS, software, machine, carrier, forensic and assessment vendors

title: Group: provider FedRAMP packages and customer responsibility matrices
source_system: Provider compliance portals; Group CMMC program office
what_it_shows: Provider A's government-community offering is FedRAMP authorized at High and the CUI collaboration suite at Moderate or higher; the identity SaaS (government-community offering) package covers lockout, risk-based sign-in and password handling; customer responsibility matrices for provider A and the CUI suite are on file. Physical access, media sanitization and region documentation for provider data centers are provider responsibilities under the CRM

title: Group: AI tool discovery
source_system: Procurement records; SaaS discovery; model registry
what_it_shows: AI in use or proposed: a generative AI engineering assistant add-on in the CUI collaboration suite licensed for a 300-user pilot in Aircraft Parts and Engineering Services; the in-house predictive maintenance model in both platform editions; the CAD vendor's generative design module in the GCEE; a coding assistant service in the government-community offering for platform developers; an enterprise generative AI assistant in the commercial productivity tenant (pilot for 2,000 non-CUI users); a third-party supplier risk scoring service; and proposals for AI visual inspection at plant 2 and an HR resume screening tool. The policy library has no AI standard

title: Group: cyber insurance policy
source_system: Group risk management files
what_it_shows: Group cyber insurance policy in force for 2026 with an incident response panel and claim notice terms

title: Group: board minutes, risk strategy, 2025 registers, internal audit plan and regulatory watch list
source_system: Board portal; GRC tool; internal audit
what_it_shows: Board audit and risk committee minutes for 2025 and Q1 2026 show quarterly cyber reports; the risk management strategy and 2025 group and division registers are on file; the internal audit charter and 2026 plan cover the annual common control assessment and division samples; the GRC team's regulatory watch list tracks proposed rules such as CIRCIA and the FAR CUI rule

title: Group: code of conduct, sanctions procedure and 2025 sanctions log
source_system: Group HR and legal
what_it_shows: Group code of conduct and sanctions procedure; the 2025 sanctions log records cases handled under the procedure

title: Group: facility security and media records
source_system: Badge system; visitor system; group facilities security
what_it_shows: Badge access controls engineering areas with thick CAD workstations; access is logged and reviewed monthly; badges and keys are issued, recovered and audited by group facilities; engineering areas have cameras and alarms; plotters and printers that output CUI sit in controlled areas with secure print release; printed CUI at engineering centers is kept in locked cabinets; an electronic visitor system with escort runs at plants 1 to 8, with records kept 3 years. Thick workstation drives are removed or wiped before off-site repair, and endpoint drives are wiped to NIST SP 800-88 with sanitization certificates

title: Group: ERP (SYS-G4) configuration and data classification
source_system: ERP admin console (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: SYS-G4 (commercial SaaS) holds orders, purchasing and DCAA-compliant cost accounting for all divisions; it holds FCI and no CUI by policy; part numbers and order data come from the GCEE without CUI; a daily extract supports paper shipping packets and receiving logs during an outage

title: Group: CUI collaboration suite (SYS-G5) configuration
source_system: CUI collaboration suite admin console (SYS-G5)
what_it_shows: Email, file storage and chat in a government-community SaaS offering (FedRAMP authorized at Moderate or higher), integrated with the GCEE; external email is allowed with recipient warnings and data loss rules

title: Group: FOCI records, consolidated SF 328 and facility clearance register
source_system: Group security office
what_it_shows: One consolidated SF 328 for the corporate family; no DCSA determination of foreign ownership, control or influence. Facility clearances are held at 2 Engineering Services centers and by no Aircraft Parts or Defense Software site; the classified systems at the 2 centers are DCSA-authorized

title: GCEE: system inventory, architecture document, asset inventory export and data location register
source_system: Cloud asset inventory; endpoint management; GCEE document library
owner: Group data and engineering platforms director
what_it_shows: GCEE components in the provider A government-community landing zone: PLM application servers and managed database, the PLM vault (about 4.8 million controlled documents), a virtual workstation pool for about 2,400 concurrent sessions, about 1,100 thick CAD workstations at plants and centers, the exchange gateway, the Program H account, key management and the backup vault. The architecture document describes defense in depth (identity, segmentation, project access, export tags, customer-managed keys). Cloud components are inventoried automatically with CMMC asset categories; thick CAD workstations at plants 4 and 7 have no CMMC asset category recorded. The data location register lists the PLM vault, Program H vault, gateway staging and backup vault. Engineering laptops reach CAD in keyboard-video-mouse mode only

title: GCEE: PLM role matrix, export tag policy, role separation matrix and access runbooks
source_system: PLM administration console; GCEE runbook library
owner: Group data and engineering platforms director
what_it_shows: PLM project spaces with roles (viewer, author, checker, release) per program; export tags (ITAR, EAR, no foreign access) enforced with the U.S.-person attribute, with a default most-restrictive tag and quarterly tag audits; key, platform and log administrators are separate roles; project, role and export-tag request runbooks; PLM stamps CUI and export markings on every released document; audit records tie every action to a named user or service account, and object-level read and write logs go to the SIEM

title: GCEE: SSP v2.0, plant enclave SSPs and tailoring register
source_system: GCEE document library
owner: Group data and engineering platforms director
what_it_shows: GCEE SSP v2.0 (2024-04-30), used for the 2024 DIBCAC High Assessment; plant enclave SSPs for plants 1 to 8 covering MES, DNC and machines, with Specialized Assets and their compensating measures; the plant 4 and plant 7 annexes predate the 2025 MES upgrade; the tailoring register records the Moderate baseline tailored for SP 800-171 Rev. 2

title: GCEE: flow register, interconnection register, external service register and gateway configuration
source_system: GCEE registers; managed file transfer console
what_it_shows: Approved flow paths: MES release push to plants 1 to 8 over FIPS-validated VPNs, the HPC transfer, the exchange gateway with per-partner folders and an allow-list of partner identities (partner users sign in through their own federation or gateway accounts with MFA), and the CUI suite. A daily export of Aircraft Parts sustainment data (CUI) to SYS-D4 has run since 2025 as an intercompany service; the external service register lists provider A and PLM vendor support with CRMs and has no CSP review of SYS-D4. The interconnection register has agreements for SYS-D1, the CUI suite and partner gateways, and none for the HPC cluster link (2026) or the SYS-D4 export. The external systems register lists prime portals and gateway partners

title: GCEE: contingency plan v3, recovery runbook and 2026-03 restore test report
source_system: GCEE continuity library
owner: Group data and engineering platforms director
what_it_shows: GCEE contingency plan v3 with the paired provider A region as the alternate site; PLM restore is tested twice a year, last in 2026-03 with a full restore of a PLM project vault in the paired region; the recovery runbook requires a manual check of released document revisions against PLM before plants resume releases; release checksums are verified on release to MES, and file integrity monitoring runs on PLM servers

title: GCEE: change records, baseline repository, pipeline permissions, image checklists and maintenance calendar
source_system: Change management system; infrastructure-as-code repository
what_it_shows: Changes go through the group change board, with a security impact analysis in every normal change ticket and emergency changes reviewed within 2 business days; baselines for PLM servers, virtual workstation images and thick workstations are defined as code; only the platform pipeline and PAM-elevated engineers can change GCEE infrastructure; image build checklists remove unused CAD add-ins; monthly maintenance windows; the lifecycle report lists no unsupported GCEE components

title: GCEE: Program H enclave configuration
source_system: Provider A account (Program H); access group export
what_it_shows: The Program H project enclave is a separate provider A account with its own vault, keys and access group, limited to named staff approved by the Program H chief engineer; its download and egress alerts use the GCEE thresholds

title: Aircraft Parts: plant and Specialized Asset inventories
source_system: Plant asset inventories (MES and maintenance systems)
what_it_shows: 9 plants, 2 of them in Florida, with about 1,140 CNC, additive and CMM machines recorded as Specialized Assets. 212 machines run unsupported controller software under a documented enduring exception. 61 machines at plants 3, 6 and 8 are loaded by USB drive from transfer workstations. The plant 4 and plant 7 inventories predate the 2025 MES upgrade. Plant 9 (acquired 2025-10-01) keeps its own records

title: Aircraft Parts: plant network diagrams
source_system: Plant network documentation
what_it_shows: Plant firewalls separate MES, DNC and machine VLANs from plant corporate networks, and machine VLANs have no internet route. Plants 6 and 8 have flat MES VLANs. The plant 4 and plant 7 diagrams predate the 2025 MES upgrade. At plant 2, Program H machines share VLANs with other programs and no intermediary devices sit in front of them

title: Aircraft Parts: MES and DNC logging, account and release settings
source_system: MES and DNC administration consoles (plants 1 to 9)
what_it_shows: MES and DNC logs reach the SIEM from plants 1, 2, 3 and 5 and stay on local servers for 30 days at the other plants. MES sign-in uses SYS-G1 where supported; MES local accounts are not disabled after inactivity at plants 3, 6 and 8, and a quarterly MES account review runs. DNC accepts programs from the release queue without checksum verification at 3 plants. Additive build files move encrypted from the GCEE and are not signed. First article inspection and operator verification apply to new programs

title: Aircraft Parts: device control reports for plant transfer workstations
source_system: Device control console (plants)
what_it_shows: At plants 1, 2 and 5 transfer workstations allow only registered encrypted drives, and drives are scanned by EDR; transfer workstations at plants 3, 6 and 8 accept any USB drive

title: Aircraft Parts: MES backup reports and plant continuity arrangements
source_system: Provider A backup vault reports; plant continuity plans
what_it_shows: Nightly MES backups from plants 1 to 8 to the provider A vault completed in Q1 2026; the hurricane plan covers the Florida plants; 3 plants can absorb urgent DoD spares work from another plant; paper travelers can be printed from the last MES extract

title: Aircraft Parts: Plant 9 acquisition and integration records
source_system: Integration program office; Plant 9 IT records
what_it_shows: Plant 9, acquired 2025-10-01, runs its own legacy network and file server holding about 6,000 CUI drawings, isolated from the group network and outside the GCEE. The legacy site VPN configuration does not confirm FIPS-validated cryptography. Visitors sign a paper log. Backups run weekly to an unencrypted local disk in a locked server room. The plant has one internet circuit. EDR was installed in 2026-02. The integration plan sets migration into the GCEE by 2027-03-31

title: Aircraft Parts: plant visitor, escort and printed drawing records
source_system: Plant visitor system; plant security procedures
owner: Aircraft Parts security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: An electronic visitor system and escort rule at plants 1 to 8; foreign-national visits are pre-cleared by the Empowered Official; printed drawings at production cells are marked, with locked shred bins at the cells

title: Aircraft Parts: MES and machine vendor support contracts and vendor session records
source_system: Aircraft Parts vendor contracts; PAM vendor session records
what_it_shows: One MES vendor support contract covers all 9 plants; MES and machine vendors reach plant systems only through PAM sessions with recording; machine vendor accounts are shared among each vendor's support staff

title: Engineering Services: engineering center inventories and field operations records
source_system: Field operations records; GFE records; laptop management console
what_it_shows: 4 engineering centers with complete center inventories; about 1,200 engineers work on customer sites with GFE and customer systems and sign in from customer networks. GFE records list equipment by site and do not record which CUI is held on GFE, customer systems or company laptops; GFE used inside the centers is not in the asset inventory. Field laptops have full-disk encryption with FIPS-validated modules and reach CAD through virtual desktops only; the 2024 supplement field rules apply

title: Engineering Services: HPC cluster and test system records
source_system: HPC and test engineering records
what_it_shows: The on-premises HPC cluster and the test and evaluation data acquisition systems joined the CUI environment in 2026. HPC nodes run the HPC vendor's image; the scheduler uses shared service keys; login nodes require SYS-G1 sign-in with MFA; urgent jobs can burst to the provider A HPC service. Acquisition units buffer data locally and transfer it to the GCEE within 1 hour of capture. HPC nodes and acquisition units have no CMMC asset categories or diagrams, and there is no SSP annex, interconnection agreement or inheritance record for them

title: Engineering Services: cleared center records
source_system: Facility security officers' files
what_it_shows: Facility clearances at 2 engineering centers with written FSO appointments and one entity-wide ITPSO; FSO procedures include FBI and DCSA reporting steps; classified systems are DCSA-authorized and separate; classified and unclassified analysis teams share buildings; the FSO log lists adverse information reports, and identity tickets to adjust CUI access exist for some of them

title: Engineering Services: subconsultant register and files
source_system: Engineering Services subcontracts files
what_it_shows: SPRS status checks started for new subconsultants in 2025; legacy subconsultants have not been checked

title: Defense Software: customer and contract register
source_system: Defense Software contract management

title: Defense Software: platform architecture, tenant isolation, recovery and key records
source_system: Architecture repository; release test records; provider A consoles
